title: Detecting and Correcting Hate Speech in Multimodal Memes with Large Visual Language Model
benchmark_measurement: Detection and correction of hateful memes, where hate speech is defined as a direct or indirect attack on people based on characteristics including religion. The evaluation measured the model's ability to identify and correct memes targeting religious groups based on stereotypes and beliefs.
findings: The LLaVA model demonstrated a limitation in reasoning when attempting to correct a hateful meme targeting Shia Muslims. While it identified the religious hatefulness, its proposed correction was culturally insensitive as it overlooked Muslim food restrictions, indicating a failure to consider relevant contextual knowledge during the generation process.
